The '''Cavaliers–Warriors rivalry''' is a [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) [[List of National Basketball Association rivalries|rivalry]] between the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] and the [[Golden State Warriors]]. The rivalry became prominent in the mid-to-late 2010s, with the two teams facing each other in four consecutive [[NBA Finals]] from [[2015 NBA Finals|2015]] to [[2018 NBA Finals|2018]]. In the four Finals, the Warriors won three championships and the Cavaliers won one.

== History ==

=== Early history ===
The Warriors dominated the early series, going 37–22 ({{winpct|37|22}}) from 1970 to 1991. The Cavaliers would win 10 straight games from 1992 to 1996 to reduce Golden State's lead to 37–32 ({{winpct|37|32}}). The two teams played each other close during [[LeBron James]]' first stint with the Cavaliers in the 2000s.

The [[2006–07 NBA season|2006–07 season]] was a memorable season for both teams, as the Warriors qualified for the 8th seed and became the first 8-seeded team to eliminate a 1-seed in a best-of-7 series, as they did in the 2007 first round against the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. On the other hand, the Cavaliers reached their first [[2007 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]], where they were swept by the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{#invoke:cite|web|url=http://www.nba.com/finals2007/series/index.html|title=Parker, Spurs Close Out Cavs for Fourth Title|work=NBA.com|date=June 15, 2007|access-date=June 15, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120111015439/http://www.nba.com/finals2007/series/index.html|archive-date=January 11, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Cavaliers' playoffs run was highlighted by LeBron James' epic performance in Game 5 of the [[NBA conference finals|Eastern Conference Finals]] versus the 1-seed [[Detroit Pistons]], with James scoring the Cavaliers' last 25 points, while sending the game to double overtime.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 1, 2007 |title=LeBron bewilders Pistons as Cavaliers inch closer to NBA finals |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270531008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222090316/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=270531008 |archive-date=December 22, 2021 |access-date=January 12, 2026 |website=ESPN}}</ref><ref name="ESPN">{{#invoke:cite|web|title=Greatest NBA playoff performances|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2012/story/_/id/8068148/nba-playoffs-top-25-performances-ever|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=December 22, 2021|date=June 20, 2012|archive-date=December 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222090320/https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2012/story/_/id/8068148/nba-playoffs-top-25-performances-ever|url-status=live}}</ref> Two years later, on January 23, 2009, LeBron James scored a game-winning [[buzzer beater]] over the Golden State Warriors, months before [[Stephen Curry]] joined the NBA.

From 2010 to 2014, James [[The Decision (TV program)|left]] the Cavaliers to play for the [[Miami Heat]] to team up with [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Chris Bosh]].<ref>{{#invoke:cite|web|last=Windhorst|first=Brian|title=A look back at the fateful 'Decision'|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/truehoop/miamiheat/columns/story?columnist=windhorst_brian&page=jamesdecision-110708|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=December 22, 2021|date=July 8, 2011|archive-date=December 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222090317/https://www.espn.com/nba/truehoop/miamiheat/columns/story?columnist=windhorst_brian&page=jamesdecision-110708|url-status=live}}</ref> The Heat went to the Finals each year, winning championships in [[2012 NBA Finals|2012]] and [[2013 NBA Finals|2013]], while the Warriors were a lottery team.<ref>{{#invoke:cite|news|agency=Associated Press|title=LeBron James, Heat dominate Thunder to win NBA championship|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320621014|website=ESPN|access-date=December 22, 2021|date=June 22, 2012|archive-date=December 22, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222175130/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=320621014|url-status=live}}</ref> The Cavaliers used their first pick in [[2011 NBA Draft|2011]] to draft [[Kyrie Irving]] from [[Duke University]].<ref>{{cite news |date=June 24, 2005 |title=Cleveland Cavaliers select Kyrie Irving as first overall pick in NBA draft |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2011/jun/24/cavaliers-kyrie-irving-nba-draft |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130930195108/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2011/jun/24/cavaliers-kyrie-irving-nba-draft |archive-date=September 30, 2013 |access-date=June 24, 2011 |work=The Guardian |location=London}}</ref> However, the Warriors won both games against the Cavaliers that season with a rookie [[Klay Thompson]] and Curry, both of whom were instrumental in the success the Warriors would experience later that decade.

The Warriors led the head-to-head series 53–50 ({{winpct|53|50}}) through the end of the [[2013–14 NBA season|2013–14 season]].

James returned to the Cavaliers during the 2014 off-season. The Cavaliers then acquired All-Star power forward [[Kevin Love]] from the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] for [[Andrew Wiggins]] and [[Anthony Bennett (basketball)|Anthony Bennett]].<ref>[http://www.foxsports.com/ohio/story/cleveland-cavaliers-big-three-bigger-with-newcomers-012115 Big Three even bigger - Fox Sports.com]</ref> The Cavaliers quickly became the favorite to win the [[Eastern Conference (NBA)|East]], as they already had an All-Star point guard in [[Kyrie Irving]] and other rising stars such as [[Tristan Thompson]].

In the Western Conference, the Warriors were a team led by their backcourt of the "[[Splash Brothers]]", Curry and Thompson, and a developed fast-paced, up-tempo offense, consisting mainly of three point shooting.<ref>{{cite news|last=Barnett|first=Phillip|title=Klay Thompson is hoping he won't lose his favorite record to Steph Curry|date=October 2, 2018|newspaper=USA Today|url=https://warriorswire.usatoday.com/2018/10/02/golden-state-warriors-klay-thompson-steph-curry-3-point-shooting-record/|access-date=February 23, 2019|quote=Klay Thompson and Steph Curry have been among the greatest shooters the NBA has ever seen ever since they stepped foot into the NBA.|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190223192018/https://warriorswire.usatoday.com/2018/10/02/golden-state-warriors-klay-thompson-steph-curry-3-point-shooting-record/|archive-date=February 23, 2019|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="Barney">{{cite web |last=Barney |first=Chuck |date=December 21, 2018 |title=Warriors' Splash Brothers meet the Bad Boys in new TV special |url=https://www.mercurynews.com/2018/12/21/warriors-splash-brothers-meet-the-bad-boys-in-new-tv-special/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190223131641/https://www.mercurynews.com/2018/12/21/warriors-splash-brothers-meet-the-bad-boys-in-new-tv-special/ |archive-date=February 23, 2019 |access-date=February 23, 2019 |work=[[The Mercury News]]}}</ref>

===2014–15 season: Warriors win first NBA title in 40 years===
{{Main|2014–15 NBA season}}
With LeBron James returning to the Cavaliers as a free agent in 2014, the team was favored to make it to the NBA Finals. The team started off the season poorly, with Love struggling in his new role and SG [[Dion Waiters]] unable to handle being relegated to a secondary role. The Cavaliers started off the season with a record of 19–20. James missed two weeks in January (which was his longest absence at the time) with back and knee injuries.<ref name="auto3">{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/12107680/lebron-james-cleveland-cavaliers-expected-miss-2-weeks |title=LeBron James of Cleveland Cavaliers expected to miss 2 weeks |website=Espn.com |date=2015-01-02 |access-date=2017-05-29}}</ref> Later that month, the Cavaliers traded away Waiters to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in a three-team deal with the [[New York Knicks]]. They acquired three-point specialist [[J. R. Smith]] and defensive asset [[Iman Shumpert]]. The team also acquired center and rim protector [[Timofey Mozgov]] in a separate trade. These players were critical for the team's return to the top of the Eastern Conference.

[[File:Stephen Curry (16454505719).jpg|thumb|right|[[Stephen Curry]] (pictured) of the Warriors won his first [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award|Most Valuable Player Award]] in 2015.]]
The Warriors started off the season 21–2, with a 16-game winning streak, which made them the early title favorites. [[Stephen Curry]] immediately became a [[NBA Most Valuable Player Award|Most Valuable Player]] candidate. Curry was improving off of last year's All-Star season. [[Klay Thompson]] became one of the best shooting guards, three-point shooters, and two-way players in the league. [[Draymond Green]] averaged about 12 points, 8 rebounds, and 4 assists per game. Rookie head coach [[Steve Kerr]] was a candidate for [[NBA Coach of the Year Award|Coach of the Year]].

The two teams split their head-to-head meetings that season, each winning on its home court.

James, Irving, Curry, and Thompson were all named to their respective [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]] teams, with Curry finishing first in the All-Star voting (1,513,324), and LeBron James finishing in second (1,470,483).<ref name="auto4">{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/allstar/NBA_2015_voting.html |title=2015 NBA All-Star Game Voting |website=Basketball-Reference.com |date= |access-date=2017-05-29}}</ref> Curry won the NBA MVP Award, averaging 23.8 points, 7.7 assists, and 2.0 steals per game, and shot 44.3% from three-point territory.<ref name="auto5">{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/curryst01.html |title=Stephen Curry Stats |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=2017-05-29}}</ref> James was third in MVP voting. He averaged 25.3 PPG, 6.0 RPG, and 7.4 APG.<ref name="auto6">{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/j/jamesle01.html |title=LeBron James Stats |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=2017-05-29}}</ref> They were featured on the [[All-NBA First Team]]. Irving and Thompson made the All-NBA team as well. The Cavaliers finished the season with a record of 53–29, and the Warriors finished the season with a record of 67–15.

The Warriors and the Cavaliers only lost five games combined in the first three rounds of the playoffs. For the first time in NBA Finals history, both teams were coached by rookie head coaches with [[Steve Kerr]] and [[David Blatt]]. The Cavaliers faced injury trouble, losing Love in Game 4 of the first round against the [[Boston Celtics]] to a separated shoulder.<ref name="haynes_04292015">{{cite news |last=Haynes |first=Chris |date=April 29, 2015 |title=Kevin Love undergoes surgery on dislocated shoulder, out 4-6 months |url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2015/04/kevin_love_undergoes_surgery_o.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150502214511/http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2015/04/kevin_love_undergoes_surgery_o.html |archive-date=May 2, 2015 |work=Cleveland.com}}</ref> Irving left Game 1 of the Finals in overtime after fracturing his left kneecap.<ref>{{cite web |date=May 30, 2015 |title=Kyrie Irving on playing alongside LeBron James: 'I became a fan' |url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2015/05/kyrie_irving_on_playing_alongs.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304063826/http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2015/05/kyrie_irving_on_playing_alongs.html |archive-date=March 4, 2016 |access-date=May 31, 2015}}</ref> The Warriors won Game 1 in a 108–100 overtime thriller. Game 2 also went into overtime, the all-around efforts of LeBron James and [[Matthew Dellavedova]]'s surprisingly stellar defense on Steph Curry took the game 95–93. James had carried the limping Cavaliers to a Game 3 win and a 2–1 lead over the Warriors.<ref>{{cite news |date=June 10, 2015 |title=LeBron James, Matthew Dellavedova steer Cavs to 2-1 lead over Warriors |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400796847 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180612184615/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400796847 |archive-date=June 12, 2018 |access-date=June 18, 2015 |publisher=ESPN}}</ref> The Warriors would win the next three games to take home the 2015 NBA Championship.<ref>{{cite news |last=Cacciola |first=Scott |date=June 17, 2015 |title=Golden State Warriors End N.B.A. Title Drought With Victory Over Cavaliers |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/06/17/sports/basketball/nba-finals-2015-warriors-win-title-beating-cavaliers.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180205072627/https://www.nytimes.com/2015/06/17/sports/basketball/nba-finals-2015-warriors-win-title-beating-cavaliers.html |archive-date=February 5, 2018 |access-date=June 18, 2015 |newspaper=New York Times}}</ref> [[Andre Iguodala]] would win the [[NBA Finals MVP]], although James averaged 35.8 PPG, 13.3 RPG, and 8.8 APG in a losing effort. However, he shot less than 40% from the field for the entire series.

===2015–16 season: Warriors' 73-win season, Cleveland's first title ends drought===
{{Main|2015–16 NBA season}}

{{See also|Cleveland sports curse}}
[[File:David Blatt and Tyronn Lue on Jan 25, 2015.jpg|thumb|260px|The [[2015–16 Cleveland Cavaliers season]] saw the firing of head coach [[David Blatt]] (left), who would be replaced by assistant coach [[Tyronn Lue]] (right).]]
The Warriors opened the 2015–16 season going 24–0, the most wins without a loss to start a season in NBA history and the third-longest winning streak in NBA history (33, by the [[1971–72 Los Angeles Lakers season|1971–72 Los Angeles Lakers]] and 27, by the [[2012-13 Miami Heat season|2012-13 Miami Heat]]). By the All-Star break, the Warriors' record was a stellar 48–4, including a pair of regular season victories against Cleveland. One notable game was on MLK day where Stephen Curry dropped 35 points en route to a blowout 132–98 victory. This was the best record at an All–Star break in league history. Curry, Thompson, and Draymond Green earned all-star selections. Golden State went on to break the [[1995–96 Chicago Bulls season|1995–96 Chicago Bulls]]' 72–10 season record by winning 73 games.<ref>{{Cite news |date=April 13, 2016 |title=Curry shoots Warriors to 73rd win, breaking Bulls' mark |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/MEMGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160414122245/http://www.nba.com/games/20160413/MEMGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-date=April 14, 2016 |access-date=April 13, 2016 |work=NBA.com}}</ref> Stephen Curry became the first unanimous MVP in the history of the NBA that year.<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 10, 2016 |title=Stephen Curry Named Unanimous Winner of 2015–16 Kia NBA Most Valuable Player Award |url=http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/curry-mvp-20160510 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160516123800/http://www.nba.com/warriors/news/curry-mvp-20160510 |archive-date=May 16, 2016 |access-date=May 10, 2016 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

Despite their regular season dominance, the Warriors struggled in the Western Conference playoffs. After defeating the [[Houston Rockets]] and [[Portland Trail Blazers]] each in five games without Curry for several games due to injuries, the Warriors were pushed to seven games by the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in the Western Conference Finals. The Thunder jumped to a 3–1 lead, but the Warriors were able to battle their way back and win the series.<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 30, 2016 |title=Curry and record-setting Warriors headed back to NBA Finals |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160530/OKCGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160601053946/http://www.nba.com/games/20160530/OKCGSW/gameinfo.html |archive-date=June 1, 2016 |access-date=May 30, 2016 |work=NBA.com}}</ref>

The Cavaliers faced some challenges in the 2015–16 campaign. Irving was recovering from a knee injury sustained in Game 1 of the previous season's Finals and would miss most of the first half of the season.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 27, 2015 |title=Kyrie Irving, Cleveland Cavaliers will not rush his return from knee injury; he may not play until January, sources say |url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2015/08/kyrie_irving_cleveland_cavaliers.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150829181959/http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2015/08/kyrie_irving_cleveland_cavaliers.html |archive-date=August 29, 2015 |access-date=August 27, 2015}}</ref> Despite some hardship, Cleveland performed well throughout the first half of the season. Halfway through the campaign, with a record of 30–11, head coach [[David Blatt]] was replaced by [[Tyronn Lue]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Fedor|first1=Chris|title=David Blatt fired by Cleveland Cavaliers; Tyronn Lue elevated to head coach|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2016/01/david_blatt_fired_by_cleveland.html|access-date=January 22, 2016|agency=Cleveland.com|publisher=The Plain Dealer|date=January 22, 2016}}</ref> The team finished the regular season with the best record in the Eastern Conference with 57 wins, sweeping the [[Detroit Pistons]] and [[Atlanta Hawks]], and defeated the [[Toronto Raptors]] in 6 games to advance to the Finals against the defending champion Warriors.

[[File:160611-D-SK590-647 (27560158656).jpg|thumb|260px|right|Inside [[Quicken Loans Arena]] in Cleveland before the start of Game 4 of the [[2016 NBA Finals]].]]
The 2016 NBA Finals saw the Cavaliers and Warriors meet for the second straight season. The Warriors won Games 1 and 2 in Oakland quite convincingly before the series moved to Cleveland. While Cleveland won Game 3 at home in convincing fashion, the Warriors took Game 4 to set up a potential series-clincher at home. During the game, Draymond Green committed a flagrant foul on LeBron James.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Branch |first=John |date=2016-06-14 |title=Cavs Still Alive After Beating Warriors in Game 5 of the N.B.A. Finals |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2016/06/14/sports/basketball/cleveland-cavs-golden-state-warriors-nba-finals.html |access-date=2026-04-13 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> After reviewing the incident post-game, the league determined that the altercation warranted a flagrant 1 foul, which put Green over the NBA's flagrant foul limit and meant that he would be suspended for Game 5.<ref>{{Cite news |title=NBA Finals: Warriors' Draymond Green suspended for Game 5 by NBA |url=http://www.mercurynews.com/warriors/ci_30006822/nba-finals-warriors-draymond-green-suspended-game-5 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160613112744/http://www.mercurynews.com/warriors/ci_30006822/nba-finals-warriors-draymond-green-suspended-game-5 |archive-date=2016-06-13 |access-date=2026-04-13}}</ref>

Kyrie Irving and LeBron James both scored 41 points in Game 5 to stay alive on the road, becoming the first pair of teammates to score at least 40 points in a Finals game.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news |title=LeBron's inspired performance drives Cavs to Game 7 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2016/story/_/id/16270831/lebron-james-giant-night-sets-stage-game-7 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211222175137/https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2016/story/_/id/16270831/lebron-james-giant-night-sets-stage-game-7 |archive-date=2021-12-22 |access-date=2026-04-13 |work=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Back in Cleveland, LeBron James continued his explosive scoring, tallying another 41-point game in a Game 6 rout of the Warriors that saw a dominating 31–9 opening sequence and a late-game ejection of Stephen Curry.<ref name=":0" /> James became the first player since [[Shaquille O'Neal]] to score over 40 points in back-to-back NBA Finals games. Curry was also the first player, also since O'Neal, to foul out in a Finals game.

[[File:Lebron post.jpg|thumb|right|260px|[[LeBron James]] (right) posts up [[Klay Thompson]] (left) at the 2016 NBA Finals.]]

With the series shifting back to Oracle Arena for the championship decider, the Warriors and the Cavaliers were neck-and-neck for most of Game 7. With a little over a minute and fifty seconds left in the 4th quarter, and with the score tied 89–89, LeBron James made a memorable [[The Block (basketball)|chase-down block on Andre Iguodala]] to save a go-ahead basket.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=soXYntMDQec|title=Top Clutch Moments from LeBron James' Playoff Career|date=May 5, 2018|publisher=NBA|access-date=January 5, 2019}}</ref> Soon after, Kyrie Irving hit a 3-pointer over Stephen Curry to give Cleveland the lead, and Kevin Love locking down Curry.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ruiz |first=Steven |title=Kevin Love came up with the biggest defensive stop of the entire NBA season |url=https://ftw.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2016/06/19/kevin-love-defensive-stop-stephen-curry-nba-finals/81841461007/ |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=For The Win |language=en-US}}</ref> In the end, they held on to win the game 93–89. This was Cleveland's first franchise title and made them first team in NBA Finals history to come back from a 1–3 deficit. LeBron James became only the third player in NBA history to have a triple double in a Finals Game 7 and was unanimously voted Finals MVP after leading in all five categories of points, rebounds, assists, steals, and blocks.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2016-06-20 |title=LeBron James becomes first player on record to lead series in points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2016/06/20/lebron-james-becomes-first-player-on-record-to-lead-series-in-points-rebounds-assists-steals-and-blocks/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230531224747/https://nba.nbcsports.com/2016/06/20/lebron-james-becomes-first-player-on-record-to-lead-series-in-points-rebounds-assists-steals-and-blocks/ |archive-date=2023-05-31 |access-date=2026-04-13 |work=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

===2016–2018: Arrival of Kevin Durant, Warriors win back-to-back titles===
{{see also|2017 NBA Finals|2018 NBA Finals}}
[[File:Golden State Warriors Small Forward Kevin Durant (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|230px|The Warriors continued their dominance with the signing of [[Kevin Durant]] (pictured) for the [[2016–17 NBA season|2016–17 season]].]]
On July 4, 2016, [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] star [[Kevin Durant]] signed with the Warriors in free agency.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Nathan |first1=Alec |title=Kevin Durant Announces Decision to Join Golden State Warriors |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2649248-kevin-durant-latest-news-rumors-speculation-surrounding-free-agent-star |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en}}</ref> He averaged 25.1 PPG, 8.3 RPG, 4.8 APG, 1.1 SPG, and 1.6 BPG. After losing the Christmas game 108–109, the Warriors got their revenge on MLK Day at home by once again blowing out the Cavaliers 126–91. After finishing 67–15, the first team in NBA history to win at least 67 games in three straight seasons, the Warriors went 12–0 in the Western Conference playoffs.<ref>{{cite news|last=Amick|first=Sam|title=Warriors sweep Spurs, advance to NBA Finals with historic 12-0 record|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/playoffs/2017/05/22/warriors-sweep-spurs-advance-nba-finals/102032554/|website=USA Today|date=May 22, 2017|access-date=May 23, 2017}}</ref> They became the 3rd team in league history to sweep all three rounds after the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] ([[1988–89 Los Angeles Lakers season|1988–89]] and [[2000–01 Los Angeles Lakers season|2000–01]]), doing it against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], [[Utah Jazz]], and [[San Antonio Spurs]], and the 1st to do so going 12–0 (the previous teams went 11–0 when the first round was best-of-five).<ref>{{cite web|title=2016-17 Golden State Warriors Schedule and Results|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/GSW/2017_games.html|work=Basketball Reference|access-date=June 1, 2017}}</ref>

In the Eastern Conference, the Cavaliers willfully made it to the Finals, going 12–1, cruising past the [[Indiana Pacers]] and [[Toronto Raptors]] in convincing series sweeps. In the Conference Finals, the Cavaliers defeated the [[Boston Celtics]] in five games.<ref>{{cite web|title=2016-17 Cleveland Cavaliers Schedule and Results|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CLE/2017_games.html|work=Basketball Reference|access-date=June 1, 2017}}</ref> James entered the Finals averaging 32.5 PPG, 8.0 RPG, 7.0 APG, 2.2 SPG, and 1.4 BPG. He shot 57% from the field and 42% from three. James averaged a triple-double in the Finals. Kevin Love also played his best basketball as a Cavalier, averaging 17.2 PPG 10.4 RPG, 1.9 APG, shooting 46% from the field, and 44% on 3 pointers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/loveke01.html |title=Kevin Love Stats |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=2017-05-29}}</ref> Kyrie Irving set a career playoff-high 42 points during Game 4 of the Eastern Conference Finals against Boston. The Warriors and Cavaliers had a combined 24–1 record entering the [[NBA Finals|Finals]], the fewest combined losses entering the Finals ever.

The series faced high anticipation as the Warriors, now dubbed as a "super-team", looked for revenge on their East coast foe from the previous year's loss. The Warriors easily took Games 1 and 2 at home, defeating the Cavaliers 113–91, and 132–113.<ref>{{cite web|title=KD keys Warriors to Game 1 rout of Cavs|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game?gameId=400954510|date=June 1, 2017|work=ESPN|access-date=June 2, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=NBA finals Game 2: Cleveland Cavaliers 113-132 Golden State Warriors – as it happened|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2017/jun/04/cleveland-cavaliers-golden-state-warriors-nba-finals-game-2-live|date=June 5, 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=June 2, 2017}}</ref> Game 3 looked to be in the Cavs' favor, until an 11–0 run by the Warriors in the closing minutes emerged, capped off by a dagger three from Kevin Durant to seal a 118–113 comeback victory.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2017/jun/07/golden-state-warriors-cleveland-cavaliers-nba-finals-game-3-live|title=NBA finals Game 3: Golden State Warriors 118–113 Cleveland Cavaliers – as it happened|date=June 7, 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=June 8, 2017}}</ref> Down 0–3, James and Irving led the Cavaliers over the Warriors to a 137–116 win, including a record-breaking 49 points in the first quarter, a Finals-high 86 points in the first half, and a record 24 3–pointers (which broke the record of 18 set by the Warriors in Game 2).<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/10/sports/basketball/cleveland-cavaliers-win-game-3-warriors.html?_r=0|title=Cavaliers Explode, Refusing to Go Quietly Against the Warriors|date=June 10, 2017|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=June 14, 2017}}</ref> Durant and the Warriors looked to finish the series back home in Game 5.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2017/jun/09/nba-finals-game-4-golden-state-warriors-cleveland-cavaliers-live|title=NBA finals Game 4: Golden State Warriors 116-137 Cleveland Cavaliers – as it happened|date=June 10, 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=June 14, 2017}}</ref> Despite early domination from James and Cleveland in Game 5, the Warriors surged ahead in the second half, fending off several late-game Cavaliers rallies, and won the title with a 129–120 victory. It was the team's second title in three years, and Durant's first championship and [[NBA Finals MVP|Finals MVP]].<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2017/jun/12/nba-finals-live-golden-state-warriors-cleveland-cavaliers-game-5|title= NBA finals: Golden State Warriors win title against Cavaliers – as it happened|date=13 June 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=14 June 2017}}</ref> The Warriors also broke a new playoff record with 16 wins out of 17 games played, with their only loss in Game 4 of the NBA Finals.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2017/06/13/sports/golden-state-warriors-win-nba-championship.html|title=Warriors Win N.B.A. Title, Avenging Themselves Against the Cavaliers|date=June 13, 2017|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=June 14, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2017/jun/12/nba-finals-live-golden-state-warriors-cleveland-cavaliers-game-5|title=NBA finals: Golden State Warriors win title against Cavaliers – as it happened|date=June 13, 2017|work=Guardian|access-date=June 14, 2017}}</ref> Both the Warriors and the Cavaliers entered the Finals with a combined record of 24–1, with the Cavaliers losing only Game 3 of the Eastern Conference Finals.

In 2017–18, Golden State won the two regular-season meetings against the Cavaliers, but struggled down the stretch with multiple All-Star injuries. For the third straight MLK day, the Warriors defeated the Cavaliers 118–108. However, fueled by the return of Stephen Curry during the [[2018 NBA playoffs|playoffs]], the Warriors dominated the first and second rounds of the playoffs against the [[San Antonio Spurs]] and [[New Orleans Pelicans]] each in five games and advanced to their fourth consecutive Finals by overcoming a 2–3 deficit against the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017–18 Golden State Warriors Schedule and Results|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/GSW/2018_games.html|access-date=May 31, 2018|website=Basketball Reference}}</ref> Cleveland also struggled during the second half of the season after overhauling their roster at the trade deadline with new, younger players.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ellentuck|first=Matt|date=February 8, 2018|title=The Cavaliers traded nearly half their team just before the trade deadline|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2018/2/8/16991762/cavaliers-trades-list-isaiah-thomas-george-hill-rodney-hood|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180609165446/https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2018/2/8/16991762/cavaliers-trades-list-isaiah-thomas-george-hill-rodney-hood|archive-date=June 9, 2018|work=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Petersen|first=Matt|date=February 8, 2018|title=Cleveland Cavaliers undergo series of reported trade makeovers|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/02/08/cleveland-cavaliers-undergo-trade-deadline-makeover#/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180609165517/http://www.nba.com/article/2018/02/08/cleveland-cavaliers-undergo-trade-deadline-makeover|archive-date=June 9, 2018|publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]|language=en}}</ref> However, they still managed to beat the [[Indiana Pacers]] in seven games, sweep the Raptors, then overcome their own 2–3 deficit against the [[Boston Celtics]] to advance to the Finals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017–18 Cleveland Cavaliers Schedule and Results|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/CLE/2018_games.html|access-date=May 27, 2018|website=Basketball Reference}}</ref> It was the first time that the same two teams in any of [[Major professional sports leagues in the United States and Canada|North America's four major professional sports leagues]] have met for a championship round four consecutive times.<ref>{{cite news|last=Stein|first=Marc|title=Warriors Dispatch Rockets, Setting Up Fourth Finals Against Cavs|date=May 28, 2018|newspaper=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2018/05/28/sports/golden-state-warriors-finals.html}}</ref>

Game 1 was close with several lead changes. James would score 51 points.<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 3, 2018|title=If LeBron James scored 51 points with one eye in Game 1, what's he need for Game 2 against the Warriors?|url=https://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2018/06/if_lebron_james_scored_51_poin.html|access-date=June 4, 2018|website=The Plain Dealer}}</ref> However, the game went to overtime, in part due to a controversial reversed charging foul call against Durant, a missed go-ahead free throw by [[George Hill (basketball)|George Hill]] with 4.7 seconds left, and [[JR Smith]] subsequently rebounding and dribbling out the clock, mistakenly believing his team to be ahead.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Golliver|first=Ben|date=June 1, 2018|title=Anatomy of a Blunder: Inside J.R. Smith's Devastating Game 1 Mistake|url=https://www.si.com/nba/2018/06/01/jr-smith-blunder-mistake-nba-finals-game-1-warriors-cavs-lebron-james|access-date=June 4, 2018|magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> The Warriors would dominate overtime, winning the game 124–114.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker|first=Mollie|date=May 30, 2018|title=New footage shows LeBron James' bench reaction to J.R. Smith's blunder|url=https://nypost.com/2018/06/04/uncut-footage-shows-just-how-badly-j-r-smith-broke-lebron/|access-date=June 4, 2018|website=New York Post}}</ref> Several minor scuffles ensued in the closing seconds of overtime, culminating in [[Tristan Thompson]] getting ejected and later fined for shoving a basketball into the face of [[Draymond Green]].<ref name="ap_game1">{{Cite web |date=June 3, 2018|title=Warriors withstand James' 51 points to win NBA Finals Game 1|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jr-smith-blunder-cleveland-cavaliers-golden-state-warriors-nba-finals-game-1-tonight-2018-05-31/|access-date=June 11, 2018|website=CBS News|agency=Associated Press}}</ref> After the game, LeBron James reportedly suffered a self-inflicted bone contusion onto his right hand after punching a whiteboard in the locker room.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 16, 2017|title=LeBron James injured hand punching whiteboard following Game 1 loss|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2018/06/09/lebron-james-injured-hand-punching-white-board-following-game-1-loss/687238002/|access-date=June 11, 2018|website=USA Today}}</ref> He played through the injury for the rest of the series, and it was not disclosed until after Game 4.<ref>{{cite web|last=Reynolds|first=Tim|title=LeBron James played with injured right hand for final three games|date=June 9, 2018|website=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/06/09/report-lebron-james-played-injured-right-hand-final-three-games}}</ref>

Game 2 was a more one-sided affair, with the Warriors winning 122–103.<ref name="ap_game2">{{Cite web |date=June 3, 2018|title=Curry dazzles from deep, Warriors take 2–0 NBA Finals lead|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401034614|access-date=June 4, 2018|publisher=ESPN}}</ref> Curry would break his own NBA Finals record with nine 3 pointers in a Finals game.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Amick|first=Sam|title=Steph Curry's historic NBA Finals Game 2 a window to Warriors before Kevin Durant|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2018/06/04/steph-currys-historic-game-2-window-warriors-before-kevin-durant/668242002/|access-date=June 4, 2018|work=USA Today}}</ref>

Game 3 was also close, as the teams exchanged leads several times. Curry struggled from the field, shooting only 3–16 (1–10, 3 pointers),<ref name="ap_game3">{{Cite web |title=Cavaliers let chances slip away _ again _ in NBA Finals|url=https://www.apnews.com/3adddd745ded44debc651e43f3507df6/Cavaliers-let-chances-slip-away-_-again-_-in-NBA-Finals|access-date=June 11, 2018|website=Associated Press|date=June 7, 2018}}</ref> while James set a record with his 10th Finals triple-double. However, Durant would lead the Warriors to a 110–102 victory, scoring a playoff career-high 43 points, along with another clutch three.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 5, 2016|title=Kevin Durant's Playoff Career-High 43 Points Leads Warriors to Game 3 Win, 3–0 Series Lead [Video&#93;|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/kevin-durants-playoff-career-high-041847783.html|access-date=June 9, 2018|publisher=Yahoo!}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=June 6, 2018|title=Durant has 43, Warriors take 3–0 NBA Finals lead over Cavs|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401034615|access-date=June 6, 2018|publisher=ESPN}}</ref>

Game 4 capped off the second time that the Cavaliers had been [[2007 NBA Finals|swept]] in the NBA Finals.<ref name="mvp">{{Cite news |last=Letourneau|first=Connor|date=June 9, 2018|title=Sweep! Warriors finish off Cavs for back-to-back championships|url=https://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Sweep-Warriors-finish-off-Cavs-for-back-to-back-12980411.php|work=San Francisco Chronicle}}</ref> In a 108–85 rout, Durant and Curry scored 20 and 37 points respectively, clinching the second consecutive and third title in four years for the Warriors, and sixth overall. Durant won his second [[NBA Finals MVP]] award, averaging 28.8 PPG, 10.8 RPG and 7.5 APG on 52.6% shooting,<ref name="mvp" /><ref>{{Cite web |last=Jack Maloney|date=June 9, 2018|title=NBA Finals 2018: Warriors' Kevin Durant named NBA Finals MVP for second straight season|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/nba-finals-2018-warriors-kevin-durant-named-nba-finals-mvp-for-second-straight-season/amp/#aoh=16299667322834&csi=1&referrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.google.com&amp_tf=From%20%251%24s|access-date=August 26, 2021|website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> while James led both teams in scoring and assists, averaging 34 PPG and 10 APG in a losing effort.<ref>{{cite web|title=2018 NBA Finals - Cavaliers vs. Warriors|website=Basketball-Reference.com|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/2018-nba-finals-cavaliers-vs-warriors.html}}</ref>

===Recent years===
Following LeBron James' 2nd departure from the Cavaliers, this time to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], in 2018, the Cavaliers entered a rebuild centered around their 2018 first round draft pick [[Collin Sexton]], and later their 2019 first round draft pick [[Darius Garland]], while retaining [[Tristan Thompson]] and [[Kevin Love]] to serve as veteran leaders. The Cavaliers struggled in their next two seasons, finishing 19–63 in [[2018–19 Cleveland Cavaliers season|2018–19]] and 19–46 in the [[2019–20 Cleveland Cavaliers season|2019–20 season]] prior to its suspension due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]]. The Cavaliers were not among the 22 teams invited to [[2020 NBA Bubble|complete the season]]. The team fired head coach Lue six games into the 2018–19 season. They hired former [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|University of Michigan]] head coach [[John Beilein]] before the 2019–20 season. He resigned midway through that season. Assistant coach [[J.B. Bickerstaff]] was named interim head coach. He became the full-time head coach for the [[2020–21 Cleveland Cavaliers season|2020–21 season]]. The Cavaliers nearly returned to the [[2022 NBA playoffs|playoffs]] in the [[2021–22 Cleveland Cavaliers season|2021–22 season]], but lost to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in the [[NBA play-in tournament]] for the 8th seed.

The Warriors returned to their 5th straight Finals in [[2019 NBA Finals|2019]], aiming for a [[three-peat|3-peat]], but lost to the [[Toronto Raptors]], 2–4.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bucks vs. Raptors - Game Recap - May 25, 2019 - ESPN |url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401131845 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190527025223/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401131845 |archive-date=2019-05-27 |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Andre Iguodala]] left the Warriors for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] and [[Memphis Grizzlies]], respectively, in the 2019 offseason (though Iguodala would eventually become a member of the [[Miami Heat]]). These losses, combined with injuries to [[Klay Thompson]] and [[Stephen Curry]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Letourneau |first=Connor |date=2019-06-17 |title=Warriors offseason plan: Who will replace Kevin Durant and Klay Thompson? |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/warriors/article/Warriors-offseason-plan-Who-will-replace-Kevin-14001865.php |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=San Francisco Chronicle |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Espn |date=2019-11-01 |title=Warriors' Stephen Curry undergoes surgery, out at least three months |url=https://global.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27983570/warriors-stephen-curry-undergoes-surgery-least-three-months |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> led the Warriors to finish an NBA-worst 15–50 in the shortened 2019–20 season and not be invited to finish the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wojnarowski |first=Adrian |date=2020-06-05 |title=NBPA reps vote to approve 22-team format to finish season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/29272443/sources-nbpa-reps-approve-22-team-format-finish-season |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

In the [[2022 NBA All-Star Game]], Stephen Curry, Andrew Wiggins and Draymond Green were selected to represent the Warriors. When Curry was announced, he was booed by all the fans in the arena, but Curry responded by dropping 50 points and winning All-Star Game MVP.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dierberger |first=Tom |date=2022-02-20 |title=Steph wins All-Star MVP with record-breaking 50-point night |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/steph-wins-all-star-mvp-with-record-breaking-50-point-night/1176481/ |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California |language=en-US}}</ref> Four months later, the Warriors returned to the Finals. Iguodala returned to Golden State after spending two years with the Heat.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Warriors Sign 2015 NBA Finals MVP Andre Iguodala {{!}} Golden State Warriors |url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/andre-iguodala-20210810 |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=www.nba.com |language=en}}</ref> Curry and Thompson returned after missing much of the prior two seasons due to injuries.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Youngmisuk |first=Ohm |date=2022-01-10 |title=Golden State Warriors' Klay Thompson scores 17 points, punctuates return with 'vicious' dunk |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/33031967/golden-state-warriors-klay-thompson-scores-17-points-punctuates-return-thunderous-dunk |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> The Warriors defeated the [[Boston Celtics]] (in a rematch of the [[1964 NBA Finals|1964 Finals]]) in six games to win their 4th title in eight years and 7th overall.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Warriors 103-90 Celtics (Jun 16, 2022) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401442535 |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref>

The teams have played fifteen games since James' departure, with the Warriors holding a 10–5 record.

Both teams qualified for the [[2023 NBA playoffs]]. This marked the first time since [[2018 NBA playoffs|2018]] that both teams clinched playoff seeds and the first since [[1998 NBA playoffs|1998]] that the Cavaliers made the playoffs without James. That postseason, the Warriors, with the help from Curry's record-setting 50-point performance in Game 7, eliminated the [[Sacramento Kings]] in seven games and would advance to the 2nd round.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andrews |first=Kendra |date=2023-04-30 |title=Stephen Curry's 50 sets Game 7 record as Warriors eliminate Kings |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/36330953/stephen-curry-50-sets-game-7-record-warriors-eliminate-kings |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On the other hand, the Cavaliers were eliminated by the [[New York Knicks]] in five games. The Warriors would again face James who was now on the Lakers. In the end, James ended their quest for back to back titles in six games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Warriors 101-122 Lakers (May 12, 2023) Game Recap - ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401545236 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230515181629/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401545236 |archive-date=2023-05-15 |access-date=2026-04-13 |website=ESPN |language=en-US}}</ref>

Early in the 2024–25 season, The Cavaliers (9–0) and Warriors (7–1) met for a marquee matchup in Cleveland. The Cavaliers hurried out to franchise record halftime lead of 83–42, also the eighth largest in the NBA's shot clock era, and tied its mark for points in a half. They went on to win 136–117 also becoming the first team in NBA history to win their first 10 games, while also scoring at least 110 points in each of them.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cavaliers 136-117 Warriors (Nov 8, 2024) Game Recap |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401704754 |access-date=2025-01-17 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref> The Cavaliers would go on to win their next 5 games starting 15-0, second only to the 2016 Warriors who started 24–0. Also of note is that the Cavaliers head coach [[Kenny Atkinson]], who was an assistant coach for the Warriors the previous year (and won a title with them in 2022), became the first coach to go undefeated in his first 15 games with a new team.

LeBron James and Kevin Durant would face again in the [[2026 NBA playoffs|2026 playoffs]], this time with Durant on the [[Houston Rockets]]. The Lakers eliminated the Rockets in six games of the first round.
